entities.name: Adam Bargielski
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Adam Bargielski (1903–1941) was a Polish Catholic priest martyred by the Nazis during the German occupation of Poland, one of thousands of Polish clergy systematically murdered in the campaign to destroy Polish national and religious leadership. Born in the Łomża region, he was ordained in the Diocese of Łomża and served as a parish priest in northeastern Poland.

When Germany invaded Poland in September 1939, the Nazis moved immediately to neutralise the Catholic clergy, whom they identified as the backbone of Polish national resistance. Bargielski was arrested in the systematic roundups of priests that accompanied the occupation and was murdered at Działdowo (Soldau) transit camp in 1941. He was among 108 Polish martyrs of World War II beatified by Pope John Paul II in Warsaw on 13 June 1999.

His beatification situated him within the extraordinary witness of Polish Catholicism under totalitarian assault—a Church that faced simultaneous persecution from both Nazi and Soviet powers between 1939 and 1945. The 1999 beatification ceremony, conducted on Polish soil by a Polish pope, represented one of the most powerful acts of national and religious memory in the postwar Church. Bargielski's martyrdom exemplifies the fusion of Catholic priesthood with Polish national identity that defined the Church's role in the twentieth-century Polish experience.
